title: EXP-134 — Mock Inventory Data Layer: FX_InventoryItems SQL Table and IDO
objective: Create exactly one tenant-wide SQL table dbo.FX_InventoryItems and one corresponding IDO FX_InventoryItems using the supported Data Maintenance Wizard, under existing IDO project FX_HelloWorldProject01, with table alias fxinv. Configure six business properties matching the operator-specified MockInventory reference: FX_Item String(50), primary key and required; FX_Description String(255); FX_Warehouse String(100); FX_QuantityOnHand Decimal(12,2); FX_ReorderLevel Decimal(12,2); and FX_Location String(100). Choose Data Type and Length directly in the wizard without Property Classes, leave Label String IDs blank unless required, and leave Create Scripts unchecked. Execute Finish once, decline the optional Form creation, inspect the resulting IDO and physical SQL table, check in the IDO once if required, then close and reopen the IDOs and Sql Tables Forms to verify recovery. Record decisive evidence and stop without creating records or Forms.

acceptance_checks.description: Preflight screenshots identify the exact authenticated account, DEFAULT configuration and Designer User scope. Evidence also identifies the existing FX_HelloWorldProject01. No mutation occurs before all required gates pass.

Before wizard mutation, separate supported IDOs and Sql Tables exact-name queries for FX_InventoryItems each return a settled zero-row result after one criteria entry and F4. Evidence captures both query states and demonstrates that the queries executed successfully. Ambiguous or expired results block creation.

Pre-Finish wizard evidence identifies FX_HelloWorldProject01, IDO/table name FX_InventoryItems, alias fxinv and exactly six business-property rows. All six Data Type, Length, key and required settings match the specification; Decimal precision is 2 wherever the wizard exposes it. Property Class and Label String ID fields are blank, Create Scripts is unchecked, and no unexpected object creation is selected.

Exactly one wizard Finish is recorded and the resulting product UI visibly reports successful table and IDO creation. The optional Create Form prompt is answered No once if displayed. No second Finish or wizard-creation attempt occurs.

Post-creation IDOs readback identifies exactly FX_InventoryItems under FX_HelloWorldProject01 with base table FX_InventoryItems, alias fxinv and six required business properties. Captured property rows establish names, supported types, lengths and the primary-key/required attributes. Any UI limitations are recorded explicitly.

Sql Tables and Sql Columns readbacks identify dbo.FX_InventoryItems and verify FX_Item as the required String(50) primary key, FX_Description String(255), FX_Warehouse String(100), FX_QuantityOnHand Decimal(12,2), FX_ReorderLevel Decimal(12,2) and FX_Location String(100), or their visibly equivalent physical SQL types. Automatically generated system columns are inventoried separately. Missing or unreadable physical types remain qualified rather than assumed.

The new IDO's final project and checkout state is captured. If it was checked out after creation, exactly one successful check-in is observed, with the resulting revision and Locked By state recorded. If already checked in, zero check-in actions are performed and the existing state is evidenced.

Both maintenance Forms undergo an ordinary close and reopen. After reopening, exact-name queries independently retrieve FX_InventoryItems and the previously verified IDO/table definitions. Evidence compares post-reopen values with the pre-close baseline and shows no unsaved-change prompt or unresolved error. The finding is limited to observed UI-level recovery.

A cumulative action audit establishes one wizard Finish, no duplicate creation, at most one new-IDO check-in, no inventory-record creation, no editor Form, no metadata unload, no FormSync, no generated-script execution and no non-FX_ business-object mutation. Any session recovery or deviation is enumerated with its exact scope and evidence.

Evidence under evidence/EXP-134/ contains concise preflight, pre-Finish, creation, IDO readback, SQL readback, check-in and close/reopen proof, plus a final acceptance matrix identifying passed, failed and qualified checks. A repository change inventory distinguishes experiment-authored files, automatically written browser evidence and pre-existing changes. Authoritative Git confinement remains subject to operator review.

initial_instruction: PROPOSAL ONLY — do not execute before operator approval. On approval, configure worker_tool_policy deny_browser_javascript=true. Start with AGENTS.md, the operator-approved EXP-134 specification, the relevant accepted wizard records and the inventory-property reference. T1 is read-only: establish the correct account, DEFAULT configuration, User editing scope, live maintenance surfaces, existing FX_ project and two independent exact-name absence gates through criteria-field entry followed by F4. Capture decisive screenshots before allowing any wizard action. If all gates pass, report and await the next bounded task. The only planned mutation is a single Data Maintenance Wizard execution producing one matching FX_ SQL table and IDO with six specified properties; subsequent verification, conditional check-in and close/reopen recovery are separately bounded steps. Never open Property Class lookup, create additional artifacts, repeat an ambiguous Finish or widen recovery scope. Allow one fresh snapshot and one corrected inspection per task, then report a blocker. Keep records and evidence confined to the new experiment.
notes: Proposed by the coordinator after run R-20261025-234739-gn7q. Rationale: EXP-133 established an accepted, single-run FX_LoginPortal runtime bridge. The next dependency for the inventory dashboard is a dedicated FX_-owned data layer. EXP-071-R2 and EXP-049 provide previously observed Data Maintenance Wizard routes for creating SQL tables and IDOs. One wizard operation creating exactly one FX_InventoryItems table and its matching IDO is the smallest useful next step. This experiment deliberately excludes inventory records, Forms and dashboard integration.
